summary: Session-affinity shard miss causing slow prefix lookup and timeouts on replayed conversational turns
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC LexiChat (dedicated tenancy) reports intermittent 30s request timeouts and p99 latency spikes on conversational replay (user resends identical turn). Impact: multiple customer requests hit streaming timeouts and 504s, affecting production traffic for two primary models. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool 'lexichat-eu1-ded-01'. Observed behavior: identical prompts that previously returned in <500ms are occasionally taking 2-30s or timing out; spikes correlate with repeat/replayed conversational turns. Expected behavior: repeat prompts should benefit from KV/prefix cache warm path and return within normal latency SLOs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's session_id and conversation turn payload (supplied in logs). 2) Send initial prompt A; observe normal latency. 3) Immediately send identical prompt A again (replay). 4) Observe second request sometimes goes to cold path and experiences 1-30s prefix lookup/sync wait and may timeout. Repro rate ~8-12% during incident window.
observed_logs_and_traces: Trace IDs: x-req-id=6f3a2c8b, 6f3a2c8c, 6f3a2c8d. Example spans: prefix-lookup p95=48ms p99=1.2s; kv-backfill remote-read 95th=900ms; router-fallback wait 18s before routing to fallback variant. Upstream 504s at edge for request with trace 6f3a2c8d. Logs show 'shardmap:cache-miss' followed by 'prefetch:scheduled-backfill' and later 'session-affinity:remapped->remote-shard'.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV/prefix cache warm path misfired leading to backfill and cross-shard remote reads. We reproduced locally using customer's session token and observed that session-affinity cookie expired and the request was routed to a different serving node which did not have the in-memory prefix index, triggering a remote KV backfill. Timeline: 2026-03-09 21:45 UTC deploy of routing change (sticky-affinity TTL reduced to 20s) coincides with start of regression. Observed frequent 'shardmap-resync' logs. SRE ran targeted trace sampling and confirmed increased remote shard reads during incidents. CPU on serving nodes was within normal bounds; bottleneck is remote KV read latency and throttling on backfill path.
hypotheses: 1) Recent routing change reduced session-affinity TTL causing more cross-node routing and prefix cache misses. 2) Prefetch throttle combined with shardmap race causes serialized backfill operations and queuing. 3) For replayed identical turns, prefix-key normalization edge-case maps to different cache keys under new routing path (less likely but still possible).
mitigations_and_workarounds: 1) Immediate: revert sticky-affinity TTL to previous value (rolled back on 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC) which reduced incident rate by ~70%. 2) Short-term: enable 'prefer-local-shard' flag for LexiChat pool to avoid cross-shard routing until shardmap TTL fix. 3) Customer workaround: add 250ms client-side retry with jitter for replayed turns (documented to customer).
fix_plan_and_rollout_notes: Proposed permanent fix: increase shardmap cache TTL to 5m, add a fast-path check in router to prefer existing in-memory prefix index, and reduce prefetch serialization for backfills (allow limited parallel backfills per node). PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/7890. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated customer pools -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with monitoring thresholds for p99 prefix lookup and KV backfill rate.
resolution: Patch PR merged and canary started on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Early canary metrics: p99 prefix lookup dropped from 1.2s to 120ms on canary nodes, incident frequency for LexiChat dropped ~92% during trial. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-13 pending final validation. Postmortem follow-up: add an automated alert for shardmap-resync rate and a regression test for session-affinity TTL changes.
